slice.name: repository-transport duplicate-create idempotency fail-closed probe
slice.tested_scope: Replay an already-existing immutable role-local reproduction artifact path through the actually exposed Chat GitHub create-file surface, without supplying an update SHA, to test whether a duplicate scheduled invocation can create or overwrite the same repository effect. Verify the existing artifact remains byte-identity-addressed by the same blob after the rejected replay. This scope tests GitHub Contents repository-transport duplicate-effect protection only; it does not establish idempotency of arbitrary production side effects.

assessment.claim: For the exact GitHub Contents immutable-artifact replay scope, the exposed Chat repository create path fails closed on an existing path rather than silently duplicating or overwriting the committed effect, and the original blob remained unchanged after the rejected replay.
limitations: The observed 422 is a GitHub Contents/create-file precondition result, not evidence that external production actions are idempotent.
No production effect server, browser/GUI action, workflow dispatch, payment, deployment, or other external side effect was exercised.
No authentic rate-limit recovery or real account quota exhaustion was observed.
This slice is not Phase-1 acceptance or completion evidence by itself.

continuation.next_action: On the next reproducibility_auditor invocation, reconstruct current downstream authority and test exactly one still-unproven boundary without repeating transport creation/readback, fail-open configuration, denial replay, synthetic 429, optional-monthly-quota-zero replay, or this repository duplicate-create guard. Prefer a directly exposed non-repository production-effect surface with an idempotency key/duplicate replay if one is safely available; otherwise capture an authentic naturally occurring missing-tool, rate-limit/resume, or distinct role-local failure boundary. Keep production-effect idempotency, authentic rate-limit recovery, authentic account-quota exhaustion, richer-mode computation parity, and global Phase-1 acceptance unresolved unless directly evidenced.
